# 1.) Summary of responses/what's presented: Include table w/residency status. Total # submissions (include completes and partials), removed non-resident/visitor (include #) surveys for this purpose 

```{r}

Response.type <- c("Complete","Partial - retained","Partial - no data/dropped")

Res.responses <- as.data.frame(table(ResidentSurvey.dat$Response.status))
Nonres.responses <- as.data.frame(table(NonResidentSurvey.dat$Response.status))

Res.responses <- c(Res.responses$Freq[1],Res.responses$Freq[2],length(remove_ids))
Nonres.responses <- c(Nonres.responses$Freq[1],1,3) # manually examined the four non-res partial entries and determined only 1 included information

Total.responses <- cbind(Response.type,Res.responses,Nonres.responses)
colnames(Total.responses) <- c("Survey Status","Resident","Non-resident")
Total.responses <- as.data.frame(Total.responses)

data <- Total.responses
num.rows <- dim(data)[1]

# Create a summary table of total responses
table_gt <- data %>%
  gt() %>%
  # Left-justify the first/row label column data
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "left"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = colnames(data)[1])
  ) %>%
  # Left-justify the first/row label column name
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "left"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = colnames(data)[1])
  ) %>%
   # Center the rest of the table data 
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "center"),
    locations = cells_body(columns = colnames(data)[2:length(colnames(data))])
  ) %>%
  # Center the rest of the table column names
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(align = "left"),
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = colnames(data)[2:length(colnames(data))])
  ) 

# 
# Save the table as an HTML file first
gtsave(table_gt, here::here("tables", "SurveyStatusTable.html"))

# Convert the HTML table to a PNG file
webshot(here::here("tables", "SurveyStatusTable.html"), here::here("tables", "SurveyStatusTable.png"))

# Save as RTF as an alternative, which may be easier to edit in document
gtsave(table_gt, here::here("tables","SurveyStatusTable.rtf"))

```


## Summarize household population info and add columns flagging young kids and teenagers in a household

```{r}

# ensure age columns are treated as numeric
ResidentSurvey.dat <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  mutate(across(c(Under7, Age7_12, Age13_18, Age19_34, Age35_54, Age55_64, Age65_74, Age75_older), as.numeric))

# Create TotalHousehold column (sum across all age bins)
ResidentSurvey.dat <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  mutate(
    TotalHousehold = rowSums(across(c(Under7, Age7_12, Age13_18, Age19_34, Age35_54, Age55_64, Age65_74, Age75_older)), na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # TRUE if any household members are Under 13 (Under7 or Age7_12 > 0)
    HouseholdUnder13 = (Under7 > 0 | Age7_12 > 0),

    # TRUE if any household members are age 13–18
    Household13_18 = (Age13_18 > 0)
  )

```


## Load region and age-specific 2020 census data and create/save summary table

```{r}
# include 2020 census data from Kevin (County GIS)
# summarize census data across all age groups by City.area, and for those over 18; create summary table

Census.dat <- read.csv(here("data","AgeCensusDataDetailed.csv"))

# Define age group columns
all_age_cols <- c("Under_7", "Age_7_12", "Age_13_18", "Age_19_34", "Age_35_54", "Age_55_64", "Age_65_74", "Age_75_plus")
adult_age_cols <- c("Age_19_34", "Age_35_54", "Age_55_64", "Age_65_74", "Age_75_plus")

# Convert to numeric and calculate row-wise totals
Census.dat[all_age_cols] <- lapply(Census.dat[all_age_cols], as.numeric)
Census.dat <- Census.dat %>%
  mutate(
    CensusTotal = rowSums(select(., all_of(all_age_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    CensusOver18   = rowSums(select(., all_of(adult_age_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Group and summarize by City.area
CensusCityAreaSummary <- Census.dat %>%
  group_by(City.area) %>%
  summarise(
    CensusTotal = sum(CensusTotal, na.rm = TRUE),
    CensusOver18   = sum(CensusOver18, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    PropCensusTotal = CensusTotal/ sum(CensusTotal),
    PropCensusOver18   = CensusOver18 / sum(CensusOver18)
  ) %>%
  arrange(City.area)

write.csv(CensusCityAreaSummary,file="CensusCityAreaSummary.csv")


#Note from email from Kevin to Diane on 3/11 regarding West End census numbers: "Using the Washington Office of Financial Management (OFM) adjusted redistricting data it brings the West End population down to 458 people or 1.4% with the inmate population moved to last known residence. The unadjusted West End population was 776."

```

## Creates data columns with Geographic and Area-specific weights
```{r}
# Weighting responses by Geography and Age combined

# Load census data again (enables running this section independently)
survey_data <- ResidentSurvey.dat
census_data <- read.csv(here("data","AgeCensusDataDetailed.csv"))

# Filter out rows with missing Age or City.area
survey_clean <- survey_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Age), !is.na(City.area))

# Map survey age bins to census column names
age_bin_map <- c(
  "18-34" = "Age_19_34",
  "35-54" = "Age_35_54",
  "55-64" = "Age_55_64",
  "65-74" = "Age_65_74",
  "75+"   = "Age_75_plus"
)

survey_clean <- survey_clean %>%
  mutate(AgeBin = recode(Age, !!!age_bin_map))

# Count responses by City.area × AgeBin
survey_counts <- survey_clean %>%
  group_by(City.area, AgeBin) %>%
  summarise(SurveyCount = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Reshape census data to long format
census_long <- census_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -City.area, names_to = "AgeBin", values_to = "PopulationCount")

# Join survey counts with census and compute weights
weights_df <- census_long %>%
  left_join(survey_counts, by = c("City.area", "AgeBin")) %>%
  mutate(SurveyCount = ifelse(is.na(SurveyCount) | SurveyCount == 0, 1, SurveyCount),
         Weight = PopulationCount / SurveyCount)

# Join weights back to the survey data
survey_weighted <- survey_clean %>%
  left_join(weights_df %>% select(City.area, AgeBin, Weight), by = c("City.area", "AgeBin"))

```

## Creates data columns with Geographic and Area-specific weights for those who respondend to the tax question specifically

```{r}
# Load census data (if not already loaded)
census_data <- read.csv(here("data", "AgeCensusDataDetailed.csv"))

# Filter survey to only valid TaxSupport responses and complete Age/City.area
survey_tax <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  filter(
    TaxSupport %in% c("Yes", "No", "I don't know/need more information"),
    !is.na(Age),
    !is.na(City.area)
  )

# Map survey Age values to census AgeBin column names
age_bin_map <- c(
  "18-34" = "Age_19_34",
  "35-54" = "Age_35_54",
  "55-64" = "Age_55_64",
  "65-74" = "Age_65_74",
  "75+"   = "Age_75_plus"
)

survey_tax <- survey_tax %>%
  mutate(AgeBin = recode(Age, !!!age_bin_map))

# Count tax support respondents by City.area × AgeBin
survey_tax_counts <- survey_tax %>%
  group_by(City.area, AgeBin) %>%
  summarise(SurveyCount = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Reshape census data to long format
census_long <- census_data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -City.area, names_to = "AgeBin", values_to = "PopulationCount")

# Join census and survey counts, and calculate weights
tax_weights_df <- census_long %>%
  left_join(survey_tax_counts, by = c("City.area", "AgeBin")) %>%
  mutate(
    SurveyCount = ifelse(is.na(SurveyCount) | SurveyCount == 0, 1, SurveyCount),  # avoid divide-by-zero
    Weight = PopulationCount / SurveyCount
  )

# Join weights back to tax-support respondent data only
survey_tax_weighted <- survey_tax %>%
  left_join(tax_weights_df %>% select(City.area, AgeBin, Weight), by = c("City.area", "AgeBin"))


```


# 2.) In which city or area do you live?

```{r}
# Question 2 - in which city or area do you live

# Clean City.area field and remove ambiguous entries
Q2.dat <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  filter(City.area != "" & !is.na(City.area)) 

# Define age group columns
all_age_cols <- c("Under7", "Age7_12", "Age13_18", "Age19_34", "Age35_54", "Age55_64", "Age65_74", "Age75_older")
adult_age_cols <- c("Age19_34", "Age35_54", "Age55_64", "Age65_74", "Age75_older")

# Convert to numeric and calculate row-wise totals
Q2.dat[all_age_cols] <- lapply(Q2.dat[all_age_cols], as.numeric)
Q2.dat <- Q2.dat %>%
  mutate(
    TotalRepresented = rowSums(select(., all_of(all_age_cols)), na.rm = TRUE),
    TotalRepOver18   = rowSums(select(., all_of(adult_age_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Group and summarize by City.area
CityAreaSummary <- Q2.dat %>%
  group_by(City.area) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalRepresented = sum(TotalRepresented, na.rm = TRUE),
    TotalRepOver18   = sum(TotalRepOver18, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    PropRepresented = TotalRepresented / sum(TotalRepresented),
    PropRepOver18   = TotalRepOver18 / sum(TotalRepOver18)
  ) %>%
  arrange(City.area)

#write.csv(CityAreaSummary,file="SurveyCityAreaSummary.csv")

#create figures of side-by-side comparisons of census vs survey representation by area
# first plot by ALL age groups
# Prepare the combined dataset
survey_area_allages <- CityAreaSummary %>% 
  select(City.area, PropRepresented) %>% 
  mutate(DataSource = "Survey") %>% 
  rename(Proportion = PropRepresented)

census_area_allages <- CensusCityAreaSummary %>% 
  select(City.area, PropCensusTotal) %>% 
  mutate(DataSource = "Census") %>% 
  rename(Proportion = PropCensusTotal) 

survey_census_area_allages <- rbind(survey_area_allages, census_area_allages)

# Add percentage labels
survey_census_area_allages <- survey_census_area_allages %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(round(Proportion * 100, 1), "%"))

# Create plot with percentage labels
plot <- ggplot(survey_census_area_allages, aes(x = City.area, y = Proportion, fill = DataSource)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) + 
  geom_text(aes(label = label),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 2.5,
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1), limits = c(0, max(survey_census_area_allages$Proportion) + 0.05)) +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Percent Distribution by Geographic Area",
    subtitle = "Survey Respondents vs. Census",
    x = "",
    y = "Area Distribution (%)",
    fill = "Data Source"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12)
  )

# save figure with fixed dimensions to standardize w/others
ggsave(here("figures","Census_Survey_Area_Fig_AllAges.png"), plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)

# IF NEEDED BY VOTING POPULATION
#create figures of side-by-side comparisons of census vs survey representation by area
# plot by ages over 18 and over
survey_area_over18 <- CityAreaSummary %>% 
  select(City.area,PropRepOver18) %>% 
  mutate(DataSource = "Survey") %>% 
  rename(Proportion = PropRepOver18)

census_area_over18 <- CensusCityAreaSummary %>% 
  select(City.area, PropCensusOver18) %>% 
  mutate(DataSource = "Census")%>% 
  rename(Proportion = PropCensusOver18)

survey_census_area_over18 <- rbind(survey_area_over18,census_area_over18)
  
```

# 4.) What is your age?

# create figure of survey age distribution alongside census age distribution, using respondent ages only

```{r}
# Q4: What is your age? question

Q4.dat <- filter(ResidentSurvey.dat, Age != "")

# Summarize Age Census Data and summarize to align with survey age bins
CensusAgeTotals <- Census.dat %>%
  summarise(
    Under_7 = sum(Under_7, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_7_12 = sum(Age_7_12, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_13_18 = sum(Age_13_18, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_19_34 = sum(Age_19_34, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_35_54 = sum(Age_35_54, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_55_64 = sum(Age_55_64, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_65_74 = sum(Age_65_74, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_75_plus = sum(Age_75_plus, na.rm = TRUE)
  )


# Count the occurrences of each unique 'City.area'
age_counts <- as.data.frame(table(ResidentSurvey.dat$Age))
colnames(age_counts) <- c("Age", "Respondents")

survey_age_counts <- age_counts %>%
 mutate(Age = as.character(Age),  # Convert to character
        Age = ifelse(Age == "18-34", "18-34*", Age))%>%  # Modify the specific row
        mutate(Proportion = Respondents/sum(Respondents))%>%
        mutate(DataSource = "Survey")

# reformat census age distribution data
census_totals <- c(CensusAgeTotals$Age_19_34,CensusAgeTotals$Age_35_54,CensusAgeTotals$Age_55_64,CensusAgeTotals$Age_65_74,CensusAgeTotals$Age_75_plus)

census_age_counts <- data.frame(survey_age_counts$Age, census_totals)

census_age_counts <- census_age_counts %>%
    rename(Age = survey_age_counts.Age) %>%
    rename(Respondents = census_totals) %>%
    mutate(Proportion = Respondents/sum(Respondents))%>%
    mutate(DataSource = "Census")

survey_census_ages <- rbind(census_age_counts,survey_age_counts)

# Add percentage labels
survey_census_ages <- survey_census_ages %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(round(Proportion * 100, 0), "%"))

#create barplot comparing survey and census age distribution (of respondents)
plot <- ggplot(survey_census_ages, aes(x = Age, y = Proportion, fill = DataSource)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +  # Dodge to separate the bars
    geom_text(aes(label = label),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 4,
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +  # Colorblind-friendly palette
  labs(title = "Percent Distribution by Age",
       subtitle = "Survey Respondents vs. Census",
       x = "",
       y = "Age Distribution (%)",
       fill = "Data Source") +  # Add a legend title for clarity
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
    )
    
# save figure with fixed dimensions to standardize w/others
ggsave(here("figures","Age_Distribution_Fig.png"), plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)


```

# create a figure of survey age distribution alongside census age distribution, using HOUSEHOLD age info

```{r}

# Summarize Census Age Data to align with survey age bins
CensusAgeTotals <- Census.dat %>%
  summarise(
    Under_7      = sum(Under_7, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_7_12     = sum(Age_7_12, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_13_18    = sum(Age_13_18, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_19_34    = sum(Age_19_34, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_35_54    = sum(Age_35_54, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_55_64    = sum(Age_55_64, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_65_74    = sum(Age_65_74, na.rm = TRUE),
    Age_75_plus  = sum(Age_75_plus, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Summarize Survey Household Age Data
survey_age_counts <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  summarise(
    `Under 7`  = sum(Under7, na.rm = TRUE),
    `7–12`     = sum(Age7_12, na.rm = TRUE),
    `13–18`    = sum(Age13_18, na.rm = TRUE),
    `19–34`    = sum(Age19_34, na.rm = TRUE),
    `35–54`    = sum(Age35_54, na.rm = TRUE),
    `55–64`    = sum(Age55_64, na.rm = TRUE),
    `65–74`    = sum(Age65_74, na.rm = TRUE),
    `75+`      = sum(Age75_older, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Age", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(DataSource = "Survey")

# Reformat Census Age Data to match survey structure
census_age_counts <- CensusAgeTotals %>%
  rename(
    `Under 7`  = Under_7,
    `7–12`     = Age_7_12,
    `13–18`    = Age_13_18,
    `19–34`    = Age_19_34,
    `35–54`    = Age_35_54,
    `55–64`    = Age_55_64,
    `65–74`    = Age_65_74,
    `75+`      = Age_75_plus
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Age", values_to = "Count") %>%
  mutate(DataSource = "Census")

# Combine both datasets
age_distribution_df <- bind_rows(survey_age_counts, census_age_counts) %>%
  group_by(DataSource) %>%
  mutate(Proportion = Count / sum(Count)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(label = paste0(round(Proportion * 100, 0), "%"))

# Ensure age bins are ordered youngest to oldest
age_labels <- c("Under 7", "7–12", "13–18", "19–34", "35–54", "55–64", "65–74", "75+")
age_distribution_df$Age <- factor(age_distribution_df$Age, levels = age_labels)

# Create the plot
plot <- ggplot(age_distribution_df, aes(x = Age, y = Proportion, fill = DataSource)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            vjust = -0.5,
            size = 4,
            fontface = "bold") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Percent Distribution by Age",
       subtitle = "Household Data from Survey vs Census",
       x = "",
       y = "Population Distribution (%)",
       fill = "Data Source") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )

# Save the figure
ggsave(here("figures", "Age_Distribution_FullHouseholds_Fig.png"), plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)
```

# create figure of respondent age distribution alongside census age distribution


#create table summarizing ages represented in survey

```{r}
# Define age bins
all_age_cols <- c("Under7", "Age7_12", "Age13_18", "Age19_34", "Age35_54", "Age55_64", "Age65_74", "Age75_older")
adult_age_cols <- c("Age19_34", "Age35_54", "Age55_64", "Age65_74", "Age75_older")

# Prepare survey data with total household members
SurveySummary <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  filter(City.area != "" & !is.na(City.area)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(all_age_cols), as.numeric)) %>%
  group_by(City.area) %>%
  summarise(
    Survey_AllAges = sum(rowSums(across(all_of(all_age_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)),
    Survey_AdultsOnly = sum(rowSums(across(all_of(adult_age_cols)), na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Clean and prepare census data
CensusSummary <- Census.dat %>%
  group_by(City.area) %>%
  summarise(
    Census_AllAges = sum(CensusTotal, na.rm = TRUE),
    Census_AdultsOnly = sum(Age_19_34 + Age_35_54 + Age_55_64 + Age_65_74 + Age_75_plus, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join survey and census summaries
CombinedSummary <- left_join(CensusSummary, SurveySummary, by = "City.area") %>%
  mutate(
    Census_AllAges_Pct = round(Census_AllAges / sum(Census_AllAges, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 2),
    Census_AdultsOnly_Pct = round(Census_AdultsOnly / sum(Census_AdultsOnly, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 2),
    Survey_Represented_Pct = round(Survey_AllAges / sum(Survey_AllAges, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 2)
  ) %>%
  select(
    City.area,
    Census_AllAges, Census_AllAges_Pct,
    Census_AdultsOnly, Census_AdultsOnly_Pct,
    Survey_AllAges, Survey_Represented_Pct
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Census_AllAges))

# Add column totals
Total <- c("Total",colSums(CombinedSummary[2:7]))
CombinedSummary<- rbind(CombinedSummary,Total)
```

# 6.) swimming ability question

```{r}
# summarize the data
library(reshape2)
Q6.dat <- ResidentSurvey.dat[,22:53]
Q6.dat <- colSums(Q6.dat,na.rm=TRUE)

# Reshape the data from wide to long format
AgeAbility <- names(Q6.dat)
long.data <- melt(Q6.dat)

#merge into a new data frame
AgeAbility.dat <- data.frame(AgeAbility,long.data$value)

# need to rename some of the AgeAbility variables so ages can be more easily separated from ability
library(stringr)

AgeAbility.dat <- AgeAbility.dat %>%
  mutate(AgeAbility = AgeAbility %>%
           str_replace_all("7_12", "7.12") %>%
           str_replace_all("13_18", "13.18") %>%
           str_replace_all("19_34", "19.34") %>%
           str_replace_all("35_54", "35.54") %>%
           str_replace_all("55_64", "55.64") %>%
           str_replace_all("65_74", "65.74") %>%
           str_replace_all("75_older", "75.older"))


# Split the variable name into AgeGroup and SwimmingAbility
AgeAbility.df <- AgeAbility.dat %>%
  separate(AgeAbility, into = c("AgeGroup", "SwimmingAbility"), sep = "_") %>%
  rename(Number = long.data.value)

# Calculate proportions within each AgeGroup
AgeAbility.df <- AgeAbility.df %>%
  group_by(AgeGroup) %>%
  mutate(Proportion = Number / sum(Number))

# Reorder AgeGroup to ensure "Under7" comes first, followed by "7.12", then the rest
AgeAbility.df$AgeGroup <- factor(AgeAbility.df$AgeGroup, 
                                 levels = c("Under7", "Age7.12","Age13.18","Age19.34","Age35.54","Age55.64","Age65.74", "Age75.older"))

# Reorder SwimmingAbility to ensure 'Non.swimmer' is first, followed by 'Beginner', 'Intermediate', and 'Advanced'
AgeAbility.df$SwimmingAbility <- factor(AgeAbility.df$SwimmingAbility, 
                                        levels = c("Advanced","Intermediate","Beginner", "Non.swimmer"))

# Create the bar plot with proportions and the reordered x-axis
plot <- ggplot(AgeAbility.df, aes(x = AgeGroup, y = Proportion, fill = SwimmingAbility)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +  # use stat = "identity" to plot proportions directly
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "",y = "Proportion", title = "Swimming Ability by Age Group") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
    )

ggsave(here("figures","Age_Ability_Fig.png"), plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300,bg = "transparent")
```

# 8.) which ones did you use? 
  
```{r}

# Filter non-empty responses
Q8.dat <- filter(ResidentSurvey.dat, WhichAquaticFacilities != "")

# Define known full facility strings (not splitting anymore)
facility_list <- c(
  "Port Angeles SHORE Aquatic Center",
  "Sequim Y",
  "Silverdale Y",
  "Port Townsend Y/Mountain View Pool",
  "Oak Harbor Community Pool",
  "North Kitsap Community Pool",
  "Olympic Aquatic Center - Bremerton",
  "Bainbridge Island",
  "Private/HOA pool (e.g. Port Ludlow, Cape George, Kala Point)"
)

# Function to extract facilities from a single response string
extract_facilities <- function(response) {
  found <- facility_list[str_detect(response, fixed(facility_list))]
  if (length(found) == 0 && str_detect(response, "^Other \\(Please specify")) {
    return("Other Pools")
  } else if (length(found) == 0) {
    return("Unmatched")  # for QA purposes
  } else {
    return(found)
  }
}

# Apply extraction function row-wise
all_facilities <- unlist(lapply(Q8.dat$WhichAquaticFacilities, extract_facilities))

# Count unmatched responses
excluded_facilities_df <- as.data.frame(table(all_facilities)) %>%
  filter(all_facilities == "Unmatched") %>%
  rename(UnmatchedFacility = all_facilities)

# Remove "Unmatched" from actual facility counts
facility_counts <- as.data.frame(table(all_facilities)) %>%
  filter(all_facilities != "Unmatched") %>%
  rename(AquaticFacility = all_facilities, Frequency = Freq) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round(100 * Frequency / sum(Frequency), 1))

# Recode for nicer display
facility_counts <- facility_counts %>%
  mutate(AquaticFacility = recode(AquaticFacility,
    "Port Angeles SHORE Aquatic Center" = "SHORE Aquatic Center",
    "Port Townsend Y/Mountain View Pool" = "Mountain View Pool",
    "Private/HOA pool (e.g. Port Ludlow, Cape George, Kala Point)" = "Private/HOA Pools"
  ))

# Reorder factor levels by descending percent
facility_counts <- facility_counts %>%
  arrange(desc(Percent)) %>%
  mutate(AquaticFacility = factor(AquaticFacility, levels = AquaticFacility))

# Plot
plot <- ggplot(facility_counts, aes(x = AquaticFacility, y = Percent, fill = "AquaticFacility")) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
   scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +  
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Percent, "%")), vjust = -0.5, size = 4.5, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(title = "Aquatic Facility Usage",
       x = "",
       y = "Percentage of Mentions") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12, face = "bold"),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
        plot.margin = margin(20, 20, 30, 20))+
  guides(fill = "none")

# Print and save
print(plot)
ggsave(here("figures", "AquaticFacilityUse_Percent_Fig.png"),
       plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

```


# 10.) aquatic amenities

```{r}
# Select the Amenities questions only for easier formatting
# Select only the AquaAmenities columns
AquaAmenities.dat <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
  select(starts_with("AquaAmenities_")) %>%
  # Automatically rename columns using gsub to format them
  rename_with(~ gsub("AquaAmenities_", "", .), starts_with("AquaAmenities_")) %>%
  select(-UsageRate)%>%
  # Replace underscores with spaces and capitalize appropriately
  rename_with(~ gsub("_", " ", .), everything()) %>%
  rename_with(~ tools::toTitleCase(.), everything())

# Reshape the data into long format
long_data <- AquaAmenities.dat %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), 
               names_to = "AquaticAmenity", 
               values_to = "Ranking")
               
# Count the occurrences of each ranking for each amenity
count_data <- long_data %>%
  group_by(AquaticAmenity, Ranking) %>%
  count() %>%
  ungroup()
  
# remove blank entries
count_data <- count_data %>%
  filter(Ranking != "")
  
# Calculate the total count for each amenity
total_counts <- count_data %>%
  group_by(AquaticAmenity) %>%
  summarize(Total = sum(n))

# Join the total counts with the count data
count_data <- count_data %>%
  left_join(total_counts, by = "AquaticAmenity") %>%
  mutate(Percentage = n / Total * 100)

# Order the data by the percentage of "Very likely" votes
ordered_amenities <- count_data %>%
  filter(Ranking == "Not likely") %>%
  arrange(Percentage) %>%
  pull(AquaticAmenity)

# Plot the stacked bar chart
plot <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = factor(AquaticAmenity, levels = ordered_amenities), 
                       y = Percentage, 
                       fill = Ranking)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +  # Use the Viridis color palette for discrete categories
  labs(title = "Aquatic Amenities by Rank",
       x = "",
       y = "Percentage (%)",
       fill = "Ranking") +
  theme_minimal() +
   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1,size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
    )
  
# Print the plot
print(plot)
ggsave(here("figures","AquaticAmenities_Fig.png"), plot = plot, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)


```

# plot heatmap/matrix to show what percentage of respondents within an age category would be very likely to use each aquatic amenity
```{r}

# Step 1: Filter AquaAmenities, clean names
AquaAmenities.dat <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
    select(Age, starts_with("AquaAmenities_")) %>%
    rename_with(~ gsub("AquaAmenities_", "", .), starts_with("AquaAmenities_")) %>%
    select(-UsageRate) %>%
    rename_with(~ gsub("_", " ", .), everything()) %>%
    rename_with(~ tools::toTitleCase(.), everything())

# Step 2: Pivot longer and filter "Very likely" responses
very_likely_data <- AquaAmenities.dat %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Age, names_to = "Amenity", values_to = "Ranking") %>%
    filter(Ranking == "Very likely", !is.na(Age), !is.na(Amenity)) %>%
    group_by(Age, Amenity) %>%
    summarise(VeryLikely = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Step 3: Total responses per Age x Amenity combo
total_responses <- AquaAmenities.dat %>%
    pivot_longer(cols = -Age, names_to = "Amenity", values_to = "Ranking") %>%
    filter(!is.na(Ranking), !is.na(Age), !is.na(Amenity)) %>%
    group_by(Age, Amenity) %>%
    summarise(Total = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Step 4: Join and calculate percent
percent_data <- left_join(very_likely_data, total_responses, by = c("Age", "Amenity")) %>%
    mutate(Percentage = VeryLikely / Total * 100)

# Step 5: Bin percentages into 5% bands, cap at 60%
percent_data <- percent_data %>%
    mutate(
        PercentBin = cut(
            Percentage,
            breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60,65,70,75,80),
            labels = c(
                "0–5%", "6–10%", "11–15%", "16–20%", "21–25%", "26–30%",
                "31–35%", "36–40%", "41–45%", "46–50%", "51–55%", "56–60%", "61–65%", "66–70%", "71–75%", "76–80%"
            ),
            right = TRUE
        ),
        # Reverse the factor levels so higher bins map to brighter viridis colors
        PercentBin = factor(PercentBin, levels = rev(levels(PercentBin)))
    )
# Step 6: Order amenities alphabetically (top to bottom)
percent_data <- percent_data %>%
    mutate(Amenity = fct_rev(fct_inorder(sort(unique(Amenity))[match(Amenity, sort(unique(Amenity)))])))

# Step 7: Plot heatmap
plot <- ggplot(percent_data, aes(x = Age, y = Amenity, fill = PercentBin)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage), "%")), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(
        option = "plasma",
        direction = -1,  # optional: reverse so bright = high
        name = "Very Likely to Use"
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Most Preferred Aquatic Amenities by Age Group",
        x = "Age Group",
        y = "Aquatic Amenity"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
ggsave(here("figures","AquaAmenities_AllAgesMatrix.png"), plot = plot)


```

```{r}
percent_data <- left_join(very_likely_data, total_responses, by = c("Age", "Amenity")) %>%
    mutate(Percentage = VeryLikely / Total * 100)

# Step 5: Bin percentages into 10% bands, cap at 60%
percent_data <- percent_data %>%
    mutate(PercentBin = cut(
        Percentage,
        breaks = c(-Inf, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60),
        labels = c("0–10%", "11–20%", "21–30%", "31–40%", "41–50%", "51–60%"),
        right = TRUE
    ))
# Step 5: Bin percentages into 5% bands, cap at 60%
percent_data <- percent_data %>%
    mutate(
        PercentBin = cut(
            Percentage,
            breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60),
            labels = c(
                "0–5%", "6–10%", "11–15%", "16–20%", "21–25%", "26–30%",
                "31–35%", "36–40%", "41–45%", "46–50%", "51–55%", "56–60%"
            ),
            right = TRUE
        ),
        # Reverse the factor levels so higher bins map to brighter viridis colors
        PercentBin = factor(PercentBin, levels = rev(levels(PercentBin)))
    )
# Step 6: Order amenities alphabetically (top to bottom)
percent_data <- percent_data %>%
    mutate(Amenity = fct_rev(fct_inorder(sort(unique(Amenity))[match(Amenity, sort(unique(Amenity)))])))

# Step 7: Plot heatmap
plot <- ggplot(percent_data, aes(x = Age, y = Amenity, fill = PercentBin)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(Percentage), "%")), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(
        option = "plasma",
        direction = -1,  # optional: reverse so bright = high
        name = "Very Likely to Use"
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Most Preferred Recreation Amenities by Age Group",
        x = "Age Group",
        y = "Recreation Amenity"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
ggsave(here("figures","RecAmenities_AllAgesMatrix.png"), plot = plot)


```

# Create Sankey plot to show change in aquatic user sentiment before/after preferred amenities

```{r}
# Prepare data for Sankey: Current vs Expected with Aquatic Amenities

library(ggalluvial)

ResidentSurvey.dat <- read.csv("ResidentSurvey.dat.csv")

# Prepare the data
Sankey_Data <- ResidentSurvey.dat %>%
    select(Current = FacilityUsageRate, Expected = AquaAmenities_UsageRate) %>%
    mutate(
        Current = recode(Current, 
                         "Don't use an aquatic facility" = "Never",
                         "Less than once a month" = "Less than\nonce/month",
                         "Several times a month" = "Several\ntimes/month",
                         "More than once a week" = "More than\nonce/week"),
        Expected = recode(Expected, 
                          "Don't use an aquatic facility" = "Never",
                          "Less than once a month" = "Less than\nonce/month",
                          "Several times a month" = "Several\ntimes/month",
                          "More than once a week" = "More than\nonce/week")
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Current), !is.na(Expected), Current != "", Expected != "") %>%
    group_by(Current, Expected) %>%
    summarise(Freq = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(
        # Flip order so "Never" appears at the bottom
        Current = factor(Current, levels = c("More than\nonce/week", 
                                             "Several\ntimes/month", 
                                             "Less than\nonce/month", 
                                             "Never")),
        Expected = factor(Expected, levels = c("More than\nonce/week", 
                                               "Several\ntimes/month", 
                                               "Less than\nonce/month", 
                                               "Never"))
    )

Sankey_Data <- Sankey_Data %>%
  mutate(stratum_fill = Current)  # Only use this for coloring the flows

# Step 2: Plot
sankey_plot <- ggplot(Sankey_Data,
                      aes(axis1 = Current, axis2 = Expected, y = Freq)) +
  # Colored flows with custom fill variable (not directly Current)
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = stratum_fill, alpha = stratum_fill), width = 1/6) +

  # Gray stratum blocks (outside aes to keep out of legend)
  geom_stratum(width = 1/6, fill = "gray90", color = "black") +

  # Stratum text
  geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)),
            size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +

  # Axis labels
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Current Usage", "Expected Usage"),
    expand = c(.05, .05),
    labels = c("Current Usage", "Expected Usage")
  ) +

  # Custom viridis fill and updated legend title
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    option = "D",
    direction = -1,
    name = "Usage Rate",
    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1))
  ) +

  # Alpha transparency mapped to flow color only
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(
    "More than\nonce/week" = 0.9,
    "Several\ntimes/month" = 0.8,
    "Less than\nonce/month" = 0.7,
    "Never" = 0.5
  ), guide = "none") +  # Don't show alpha in legend

  # Final formatting
  labs(
    title = "Expected Change in Aquatic Facility Usage",
    y = "Number of Respondents"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, color = "black")
  )

ggsave(here("figures","UsageRateChange_SankeyPlot.png"), plot = sankey_plot)

```

# Create table of tax support numbers, weighted and unweighted

```{r}

# tax support table

# Clean and recode survey data
TaxSupport_clean <- survey_weighted %>%
  filter(City.area != "", TaxSupport != "") %>%
  filter(TaxSupport %in% c("Yes", "No", "I don't know/need more information")) %>%
  mutate(
    TaxSupport = ifelse(TaxSupport == "I don't know/need more information", 
                        "Need more info", 
                        TaxSupport)
  )

# Raw counts
raw_counts <- TaxSupport_clean %>%
  group_by(City.area, TaxSupport) %>%
  summarise(RawCount = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = TaxSupport, values_from = RawCount, values_fill = 0)

# Weighted counts
weighted_counts <- TaxSupport_clean %>%
  group_by(City.area, TaxSupport) %>%
  summarise(WeightedCount = sum(Weight, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = TaxSupport, values_from = WeightedCount, values_fill = 0)

# Rename weighted columns for clarity
colnames(weighted_counts)[-1] <- paste0(colnames(weighted_counts)[-1], "_Weighted")

# Join raw and weighted tables
summary_table <- left_join(raw_counts, weighted_counts, by = "City.area")

write.csv(summary_table, file="TaxSupportSummaryTable.csv")
```

```{r}
}

  ggplot(aes(x = factor(City.area, levels = ordered_count), y = weighted_count, fill = TaxSupport)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  scale_fill_viridis(discrete = TRUE) +
  labs(
    title = "Tax Support by Area in Numbers",
    subtitle = "Weighted by Age and City/Area",
    x = "", 
    y = "Weighted Responses",
    fill = "Tax Support"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold")
  )

ggsave(here("figures", "TaxSupport_by_Area_number_Weighted.png"), 
       plot = plot_count, width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", dpi = 300)


```
